definitions.gloss: to be naughty, to act up, to misbehave
definitions.explanation: Describes childish misbehavior or playful troublemaking, typically by children.

definitions.gloss: to be wild, to raise hell, to get into trouble
definitions.explanation: When used about teenagers or young adults, describes rebellious or delinquent behavior, often looking back on it nostalgically.

examples.japanese: うちの{子|こ}はよくやんちゃする。
examples.english: My kid is always acting up.

examples.japanese: {男|おとこ}の{子|こ}はやんちゃするものだよ。
{子供|こども}がやんちゃして、{壁|かべ}に{落書|らくが}きをした。
examples.english: The kids got into mischief and scribbled on the wall.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}はやんちゃしてたな。
examples.english: I was pretty wild when I was young.

examples.japanese: {学生|がくせい}{時代|じだい}にやんちゃした{仲間|なかま}と{久|ひさ}しぶりに{会|あ}った。
examples.english: I met up with friends I used to raise hell with back in school.

examples.japanese: ちょっとやんちゃしすぎて、{先生|せんせい}に{怒|おこ}られた{思|おも}い{出|で}がある。
examples.english: I have memories of going too wild and getting scolded by the teacher.

notes:
The noun form やんちゃ can also be used as a な-adjective: やんちゃな{子|こ} (a naughty child).

When adults describe their own past やんちゃ, it often carries a nostalgic or self-deprecating tone, sometimes even a hint of pride in having been rebellious.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- やんちゃな{子|こ}: a naughty/rambunctious kid
- やんちゃ{盛|ざか}り: at the peak of mischievous age
- {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}のやんちゃ: youthful wildness
